title: SmoothFlow cost autotuner with telemetry failsafe
creator: Leila Park
description:
Goal: Build an autonomous recommendation+apply system (SmoothFlow) that proposes batching and KV-prefix caching profiles to reduce per-token cost while ensuring latency and throughput SLOs are never violated. SmoothFlow must: (1) generate workload-aware recommendations, (2) perform staged safe applies (canary cohorts, soft-apply), (3) detect anomalies and auto-revert using a telemetry failsafe, and (4) expose clear reasoning and rollback rationale for operators.

Scope and constraints: This ticket covers the recommendation engine heuristics, canary orchestration, limiter integration, SLO-aware routing hooks, anomaly detectors, and operator UX hooks (apply/rollback reason). It does NOT include new kernel-level runtime changes or new hardware scheduling policies; those are separate tickets. SmoothFlow must operate across Hosted and Dedicated modes and honor tenant isolation (no cross-tenant caching unless explicitly allowed).

Design summary: The system has three cooperating planes: Recommendation Plane, Orchestration Plane, and Safety Plane.
- Recommendation Plane: offline profiler + streaming estimator that computes candidate batching window, micro-batch sizes, and prefix-cache TTLs per model/route. Uses past 72h token/seq distribution, p50/p90 latency, and tail metrics to create a ranked candidate set with estimated cost-savings and SLO risk score. Candidates are annotated with suggested limiter thresholds (max inflight tokens, per-cohort qps, burst allowance).
- Orchestration Plane: staged apply engine that supports shadow-applying a config (no effect on production) then a canary cohort (e.g., 1% of traffic by routing tag) followed by linear ramp with soft-apply thresholds. The orchestration integrates with rollout policies in Console and can attach a rollback hook. All applies are annotated with a reason and GUID for traceability.
- Safety Plane: circuit-breakers and anomaly detectors. Circuit-breakers include token-latency fence (if p95 crosses threshold for 3 consecutive 30s windows), throughput drop detector (if committed throughput drops >10% vs baseline for the cohort), and error-rate surge detector. Anomaly detectors also run spectral analysis on latency distributions to catch shape changes even if p95 remains under threshold. When triggered, Safety Plane triggers immediate routing fallbacks (SLO-aware routing to higher-capacity or less-optimized model variants) and automatic revert of the applied config.

SLO-aware routing details: SmoothFlow tags traffic cohorts with a capability score and routes requests based on policy: prefer optimized config until latency risk > configured tolerance, then route some fraction to stable baseline (via dynamic weighted routing). Routing decisions consider region, customer tier, and circuit status. Routing adjustments are rate-limited using the same limiter layer to prevent cascading instability.

Anomaly detection technique: Lightweight hybrid: exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) for fast signal plus a simple KL divergence test between recent and baseline latency histograms for distributional shifts. Together these reduce false positives from transient spikes while keeping sensitivity to new failure modes.

Operator UX and observability: Console will show per-apply forecast (cost delta, predicted p95 delta, uncertainty band), an event timeline for canary window, and an automatic playbook message when a revert occurs (reason+GUID). All applies generate a detailed trace to the tracing pipeline (trace id in apply metadata).

Testing plan: end-to-end canary in staging with synthetic workloads that exercise short/long sequences, bursty arrival patterns, and KV cache hit/miss scenarios. Fail-open scenarios tested by injecting latency and throughput regressions to assert auto-revert behavior. Performance microbenchmarks against runtime-1.24 to confirm no negative regressions.

Success metrics: reduction in per-token cost for candidate routes (median 12% improvement on eligible traffic), zero customer-facing SLO violations attributable to SmoothFlow (no p95 regression beyond 5% of baseline), and mean time-to-detect-and-revert < 2 minutes for injected anomalies in staging.
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation engine produces ranked candidates with cost and SLO risk scores for 90%+ of model/route combos
Staged apply supports shadow -> canary -> ramp -> commit with manual and automatic rollback triggers
Safety Plane auto-reverts on p95 latency breach or throughput loss as defined and routes affected traffic to fallback models
Console shows forecast, apply GUID, and rollback rationale for each automated apply
E2E staging tests demonstrate mean detect-and-revert time < 2 minutes for injected regressions
rollout_plan: Week 1: Feature branch + unit tests + recommendation simulator; review design doc (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CO/SmoothFlow)
Week 2: Implement Orchestration Plane + canary wiring; run internal canaries on low-risk routes
Week 3: Safety Plane anomaly detectors + auto-revert hooks; integrate Console visibility
Week 4: Staging stress tests + controlled pilot on 5% of eligible production traffic; monitor closely
Post-pilot: Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% with human-in-loop approvals for new models
telemetry_and_alerting: New metric: smoothflow.apply.success_rate (per-config) - alert if < 99% over 1h
Dashboard: model/route forecast vs observed p95, cost delta, and uncertainty band
Alert: auto-revert triggered -> pager if revert_count > 3 in 1h for same model/route
